result.final_text:
## What this letter says

This letter gives the results of your knee scan. The scan was an MRI. An MRI is a scan that uses magnets to take detailed pictures inside the body. It looked at your left knee.

The scan found these things:

- There may be a small tear in the soft cartilage on the inner side of your left knee. It is at the back part (posterior horn of the medial meniscus). This is possible. A tear cannot be ruled out.
- There is no broken bone (fracture).
- One of the main knee ligaments is not damaged. It is whole (anterior cruciate ligament, ACL, intact).
- There is mild, early wear and tear on the inner side of the knee (osteoarthritis).
- There is a little fluid in the knee (small joint effusion).

Surgery is not planned at this stage.

## What you need to do

1. Mr Osei has sent you for physiotherapy. It lasts 6 to 8 weeks.
2. Mr Osei will see you again in the orthopaedic clinic in 3 months.
3. You can carry on with normal activities as far as pain allows.

## Dates and medicines

- 1 September 2026: you had the MRI of your left knee.
- 6 to 8 weeks: the length of your physiotherapy.
- In 3 months: Mr Osei will see you again in the orthopaedic clinic.

The letter does not list any medicines.

## Questions to ask your doctor

- What will happen in physiotherapy?
- What is the orthopaedic clinic?
- How will we know if there is a tear in my knee?
- What will you check at my visit in 3 months?

## When to get urgent help

The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
